1:1.t: Let us first consider what Micah signifies in Latin. It means 'Who is from God' or as we find elsewhere 'who is this man,' the son of the Morasthite, that is, the heir? Now, who is this heir, but the Son of God, Who says, All things are given unto Me of My Father; and Who, being Himself the Heir, would have us His co-heirs. And well may we say 'Who is that man?' not one of the people, but chosen to receive the grace of God, in whom the Holy Spirit speaks, who began to prophesy in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah kings of Judah. By which order is signified the course of the vision, for the progress is from the times of evil kings to that of a good king.

Micah, on whom I now desire to dictate commentaries, is third in the order of the twelve prophets according to the Seventy translators, sixth according to the Hebrew truth; and he follows the prophet Jonah, who succeeds Obadiah, and so it comes about that Amos is third, and Joel second after Hosea, who is first among all. Therefore, placed as it were in the heart of the volume, he must contain deep mysteries; and the word of God, which always descends to the prophets, descends to Micah as well, which means humility; to Micah of Moresheth, which to this day is a rather small village near Eleutheropolis, a city of Palestine. Moresheth, moreover, in our language means heir. […]

The word of the Lord which came to Micah of Moresheth in the days of Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah: which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem. Or according to the Seventy: Concerning the things which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem. The word of the Lord, then, came to Micah after Hosea, Amos and Isaiah, who prophesied under Uzziah. From this we understand that Micah did not prophesy in the times of Uzziah, but in those of his son Jotham, after whom Ahaz reigned, Hezekiah succeeding to the rule of his father Ahaz, under whom the ten tribes were led into captivity by the Assyrians. […]
Michaea [Micah]: who is here (an adverb of place), or who is this.

1:2.t:
[Passage quoted, Micah i. 2-5.]

HERE, too, in this passage the Descent of the Lord coming forth from His place is proclaimed plainly. This must mean the Word of God, Whom I have proved in the previous books to be alone God and Lord after the Supreme and Almighty God. His place you would rightly understand to be the kingdom of heaven, and the glorious throne of His Divinity, of which the prophet sang in praise of God, saying, "Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever,'' on which the Father bade Him sit as being His Only-begotten Son, saying, "Sit thou on my right hand." For I have already shewn that these words can only be referred to our Saviour, God the Word. […]
1:2.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 6, Chapter 13

1:2.t: Hear, all you peoples, and let the earth attend, and its fullness, and let the Lord God be a witness to you, the Lord from his holy temple. LXX: Hear, all you peoples, and let the earth listen, and all who are in it, and let the Lord God be for a testimony to you: the Lord from his holy house. Since according to the history the sense is plain, I leave the understanding of it to the prudence of the reader. According to tropology, however, he calls together the peoples to hear, that is, the churches of the whole world, and the earth to listen, because the earthly doctrines of the heretics have been built up in it. […]

1:3.t: Now let us also consider Jesus' statement, "I have proceeded and come from God." It seems useful to me to juxtapose to these words the following words from Micah: "Hear my words, you people, and let the earth and all who are in it pay attention; and the Lord shall be among you for a witness, the Lord from his holy house. Therefore behold, the Lord proceeds from his place and will come down and tread upon the high places of the earth, and the mountains will be shaken under him, and the valleys will be dissolved like wax, before fire and like water tumbling down in a waterfall." […]
1:3.s: COMMENTARY ON THE GOSPEL OF JOHN 20:152-56

1:3.t: "I have come down," he says, "that I may see." When responses are conveyed to Abraham, God is not said to come down, but to stand over him, as we expounded above: "three men stood," it says, "over him." But now, because the cause of sinners is being dealt with, God is said to come down. See that you do not perceive an ascent and descent of place. For frequently this is found in the divine letters, as in the prophet Micah: "behold," he says, "the Lord has gone out from his holy place and has come down and will tread upon the high places of the earth." God therefore is said to come down, when he deigns to have care of human frailty. […]

I HAVE already considered this prophecy among the passages. And I have pointed out that only from the date of our Saviour Jesus Christ's Coming among men have the objects of Jewish reverence, the hill called Zion and Jerusalem, the buildings there, that is to say, the Temple, the Holy of Holies, the Altar, and whatever else was there dedicated to the glory of God, been utterly removed or shaken, in fulfilment of the Word which said:

"Behold the Lord, the Lord comes forth from his place, and he shall descend on the high places of the earth, and the mountains shall be shaken under him." […]
1:3.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 8, Chapter 3

1:3.t: and the place of the Lord is every one in whom he finds lodging, or certainly the Son is the place of the Father, just as the Father too is the place of the Son, as the Lord Savior says: I in the Father, and the Father in me; Micah too signifies this same thing: Behold, the Lord will go forth from his place, and will come down upon the high places of the earth; and the mountains will be shaken beneath him, and the valleys will melt like wax before the fire, and like water that is carried down a steep place: for when the Lord Savior came down and set out from the Father, the high places of the earth and the mountains were shaken, and the lower parts of the valleys were melted;

Tropologically, however, the Lord will go forth from his place, by which we can understand either the Son or all the saints. For the Son himself says: I am in the Father, and the Father in me, and of the saints: I will dwell and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people. From these, then, he will go forth, not that he abandons them; for the word of the Lord also went forth from the apostles to those who heard, and yet it did not leave them; and places of this kind, that is, those which deserve to have God as their guest, rising as it were with Christ and sitting with him in the heavenly places, are set on high. Hence too he is said to come down to those who cannot hear his teaching on the mountain. […]

For behold, the Lord will go forth from his place, and he will come down and tread upon the high places of the earth, and the mountains will be consumed beneath him, and the valleys will be split like wax before the fire, like waters that run down headlong; for the crime of Jacob is all this, and for the sins of the house of Israel. What is the crime of Jacob? Is it not Samaria? And what are the high places of Judah? Are they not Jerusalem? LXX: For behold, the Lord will go forth from his place, and will come down, and will go up upon the high places of the earth, and the mountains will be shaken beneath him, and the valleys will melt like wax before the fire, and like water flowing down a slope; […]

It can also be understood thus: that because of the impieties of Samaria and the crimes of the Jews the Lord went forth from what was once his place, and said to the Jews: Behold, your house shall be left to you desolate. And he came down from the heavens, and went up upon the high places of the earth, that is, upon those who, believing out of the lowliness of the Gentiles, deserved to be lofty. And the mountains were shaken, the doctrines of the philosophers and lofty kingdoms, and those who remained lowly were consumed and crushed by the coming of the Savior; and as the Church grew and the mountains rose on high, the idols fell down into the depth. […]

1:5.t: The Lord, therefore, will come, terrible for teaching, that is, for moving the mountains and for dissolving the lowness of the valleys, because Jacob committed impiety, and Israel sin. But the impiety of Jacob is the conventicles of the heretics, which are called Samaria. And the sin of Judah, that is, of him who confesses the Lord, is nothing other than Jerusalem, in which many crimes are found. That the house of Judah, moreover, is referred to Christ, whose Church it is, we have both often said, and let us set down this for the present: Judah, your brothers shall praise you; your hands shall be upon the back of your enemies.

1:6.t: And I will make Samaria like a heap of stones in the field when a vineyard is planted, and I will pull down her stones into the valley, and I will lay bare her foundations, and all her carved images shall be cut to pieces, and all her wages shall be burned with fire, and all her idols I will lay waste; for they were gathered from the wages of a harlot, and to the wages of a harlot they shall return. For this I will lament and howl, I will go stripped and naked, I will make a lamentation like that of the dragons, and a mourning like that of the ostriches, for her wound is desperate, for it has come even to Judah, and has touched the gate of my people, even to Jerusalem. LXX: And I will make Samaria a watch-hut for fruit in the field, and a planting of a vineyard; […]

But since we have once understood Samaria as the church of the heretics, which, separated from God, has become a conventicle of the people, the Lord himself threatens that he will make her a watch-hut for fruit, a field and a planting of a vineyard. For it is much better that a useless city be overthrown, and the stones with which it had been built be pulled down headlong, and that it be prepared for an orchard and a planting of vineyards, than that it remain in a most wicked building. For when her foundations have been destroyed and laid bare, — those by which she seemed to conceal her mysteries and to have firm doctrines on which she stood; […]

1:7.t: And all her carved images, and all the riches that various kings had brought together into her, will be cut to pieces and burned with fire and reduced to nothing. For the wealth and the manifold furnishings, which had been gathered, as was thought, from the fornication of idols, will be carried off to another harlot, that is, to Nineveh, so that, just as in their own land they committed fornication with the idols which they made, so they may go to another land of idols and of fornication, that is, to the Assyrians. Thus far concerning Samaria.

1:8.t: Because of this, when their field has been turned into a watch-hut for fruit and prepared for vineyards, and the stones with which the city had been built have been pulled down into the depth, and their foundations have been laid bare, and all the carved images cut to pieces and burned, and the wages which they promised themselves with vain hope, and whatever they seemed to worship as God, reduced to nothing, because they had procured every reward for themselves from the fornication of the soul, then, understanding their former error and returning to themselves, they will lament over the things at which they used to laugh, and they will mourn over the things in which, committing fornication, they formerly in some way rejoiced. […]

And since the same wound is to reach Jerusalem — for she too sinned with a like error, forsaking her God and fashioning idols —, for that reason the prophet makes as it were a προσωποποιίαν (personification) of God, and under his own person brings in the feeling of one who laments, and says: For this I will lament and howl, I will go stripped and naked; for I have lost the ten tribes, and I will make a lamentation like that of the dragons, and a mourning like that of the ostriches. […]

1:9.t: And this Samaria of such a kind will lament and mourn for this reason: because, wounded by the arrow of the Lord and receiving the wound of the word, she will recognize her error. And not only did she herself sin, but she also wished to bring her iniquity and her error into the gates of Judah. Hence it is said of her: It has come even to Judah, and has touched even to the gates of my people, even to Jerusalem. She touched the gates, he says, by which we understand the ears. But she could not enter the middle of the city; for if she had entered, she would have made Jerusalem a Samaria. […]

1:10.t: In Gath do not announce it, do not weep with tears; in the house of dust sprinkle yourselves with dust; pass over for yourselves, dwelling of Shaphir, confounded with shame; she who dwells in Zaanan has not gone out. The house of Ezel will receive mourning from you, the house that stood by itself, for she who dwells in Maroth has grown weak unto good; for evil has come down from the Lord to the gate of Jerusalem. The tumult of the chariot of astonishment for the one dwelling in Lachish is the beginning of sin for the daughter of Zion, for in you were found the crimes of Israel. Therefore he will give emissaries upon the inheritance of Gath; the house of lying, for a deception to the kings of Israel. Still I will bring an heir to you who dwell in Mareshah; […]

Gath means winepress; those, therefore, who are in Gath, that is, in the winepress, thinking that they have gathered the vintage of the fruit of life and trodden the cluster from the vine of Sorek, are lifted up into pride, not knowing that the cluster of the land of Judea is not found in the territories of the Philistines. Do not, he says, be lifted up, you who are in the winepresses. For your vine is of the vine of Sodom, and your shoot of Gomorrah, and your grape is of bitterness, and you have a cluster of gall, and the fury of dragons is your wine, the incurable fury of asps. […]

1:11.t: Pass over for yourselves, dwelling of Shaphir, which in the Syriac and Hebrew language means beautiful. For Samaria is shown even now, situated in the most beautiful and most fertile place of Judea. It is said to her, therefore: O you who dwell in a most fertile region, since you are confounded with shame, so pass over, so be led away into captivity, that because of the greatness of your evils not even your neighbor the Philistine may hear your voice. Moreover, what follows: She who dwells in Zaanan has not gone out, which means going out, or as Symmachus renders: The abundant dwelling has not gone out, is said of the same Samaria, which is at the very doors of the Assyrian captivity, and as soon as she is moved from her borders, enters hostile land. […]

There follows: She who dwells well in her cities has not gone out, dwelling in Zaanan. This seems to me to have this meaning: You who are proud in Gath and in Bachim, in vain do you try to build a house worthy of laughter; sprinkle yourselves with dust and repent, because you wished to press out a detestable wine and to construct a building contrary to God. But the Church of Christ, which dwells well, and, possessing churches in the whole world, is joined by the unity of the Spirit, and has the cities of the law, of the prophets and of the Gospel, and of the apostles, has not gone out of her borders, that is, out of the holy Scriptures, but keeps the possession she entered upon, because she dwells in Zaanan, which Symmachus, as we said above, rendered abundance; […]

1:12.t: And she received mourning, and was struck with fear and weakened in her good, she who dwells in Maroth, that is, in bitternesses; or as Symmachus renders: The dwelling provoking to bitterness, that is, ἡ κατοικία ἡ παραπικραίνουσα, which in Hebrew is called iosebeth maroth, on account of the captivity of the neighboring tribes, because evil came down from the Lord to the gate of Jerusalem; for the Assyrian, after laying waste Samaria, came also to Jerusalem, at the time when Rabshakeh was sent, hurling insults, about whom both the fourth book of Kingdoms (2 Kings) and Isaiah write more fully. There it is said that the Assyrian king sent from Lachish to Jerusalem, and afterwards, Lachish having been taken, passed on to attack Libnah.

Moreover, as to what is brought in, For evils have come down from the Lord upon the gates of Jerusalem, the Marcionites and the Manichaeans too use this text, on the ground that the God of the law is the author of evils. Let us say that evils came down from the Lord in the way that the Savior also speaks in the Gospel: I saw Satan like lightning falling from heaven. For as there Lucifer, who rose in the morning, fell from heaven and was crushed upon the earth, he who used to send to the nations, so also these evils, which fell from the Lord and came to the gates of Jerusalem, were not evils before they fell, but because they fell headlong from the Lord, for that reason they became evils. […]

1:13.t: Therefore, O Lachish, city given over to idols, the chariot and cavalry of the Assyrians will come to you too, because in you also were found the crimes of Israel, and you were the beginning of idolatry in Judah; for through you, as through a gate, the impiety of the ten tribes migrated into Jerusalem.

After this it is written: You who dwell in Lachish: she is the chief of sin for the daughter of Zion. Lachish is interpreted πορεία ἐστὶν, that is, walking. And so these too, who went up in their chariots, and had horsemen, and only din and empty sound, to whom she who dwells well in her cities said, These in chariots and these on horses, but we will call upon the name of the Lord our God; because they moved their feet, and were carried about by every wind of false doctrine, and wished to go out from the Church, which is interpreted watchtower, that is, Zion, were the chiefs of sin for the daughter of Zion. And in her, that is, in Lachish, were found the impieties of Israel, which separated the people of God from its former kingdom. […]

1:14.t: Emissaries too will be given as far as the inheritance of Gath: Gath most wicked, and a winepress of poisons, which is built against the house of God, where there are vain houses, which were built for derision. And these vain houses were made in vain for the kings of Israel: as far as the history is concerned, for those kings whose sins are written in the books of Kingdoms and of Chronicles; but as far as anagogy is concerned, for the chiefs of the heretics and the leaders of perverse doctrines; for to them the houses are vain and built in vain. And they last only so long, until the heirs who are to be brought in by the Lord hold them.

And not only upon Lachish will the tumult and the chariots come, but also upon Gath, the chief city of Philistia, of which I had said above: In Gath do not announce it; for the Assyrian will send his brigands, whom he calls emissaries, and will possess the house of idolatry and the city of lying, which was a stumbling to the kings of Israel. As for what follows: Still I will bring an heir to you who dwell in Mareshah, he has alluded beautifully to the name; for since Mareshah means inheritance, he called the coming of the enemies into her heirs; and Mareshah, that is, the inheritance, will come as far as Adullam, a city of Judah, which Adullam is glorious among the cities of Israel. […]

1:15.t: After this there follows: You who dwell in Lachish, the inheritance will come as far as Adullam. Adullam means testimony of the draught, or of their drawing, which in Greek is expressed more significantly, μαρτυρία ἀντλήσεως αὐτῶν. We read in Proverbs: If you are evil, you alone will draw up evils. She, therefore, who dwells in Lachish, that is, on a most evil road, will come to the testimony of her own draining, which she will drain and drink down according to the measure of her works. […]

1:16.t: Make yourself bald and be shorn over the sons of your delights; enlarge your baldness like the eagle, for they have been led captive from you. LXX: Glory of the daughter of Israel, make yourself bald and be shorn over your delicate sons; enlarge your baldness like the eagle, for they have been led captive from you. What was said by the Seventy, glory of the daughter of Israel, with their addition of the daughter, the Hebrews read at the end of the preceding section. But since you wished it so, and we have once undertaken it, the necessity lies upon us of interpreting the Scriptures as they are read in the Church, and nonetheless of not omitting the Hebrew truth. […]

What happened to her we know was said through the prophet concerning Judea: Enlarge your baldness like the eagle. For the baldness of a man usually occurs only on the head, but the baldness of an eagle occurs over the whole body, because when it has grown very old, its feathers and plumes fall from all its limbs. Therefore she enlarges her baldness like an eagle, because she has lost her feathers, she who has lost her people. The feathers of her wings also fell, with which she was accustomed to fly to prey, because all her powerful men have perished, through whom she seized the things of others.

2:1.t: Woe to you who devise what is useless, and work evil on your beds; in the morning light they do it, for their hand is against God; and they coveted fields and took them by violence, and seized houses, and they wronged a man and his house, a man and his inheritance. Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I devise evil against this family, from which you shall not withdraw your necks, and you shall not walk proudly, for it is a most evil time. In that day a parable shall be taken up over you, and a song shall be sung with sweetness by those who say: We have been laid waste with devastation; the portion of my people has been changed. How will it depart from me, when he returns who divides our lands? […]

But this same thing can also be taken of the last captivity, that all things befell them because they crucified the Lord, yet in such a way that it is the edition of the Seventy translators that is expounded. For the glory of the daughter of Israel has been made bald and shorn over her once most delicate sons, and if any hair grew back afterwards, it was cut off in turn by another shaving and shearing. Then all their counsels were turned into toil, and what they devised, with mind and spirit asleep, brought them toils; and what they had done was thrown into confusion as soon as the light of Christ and vengeance appeared. […]

But if we wish to follow the third exposition, of which I spoke above, that the whole discourse is directed to the human soul, which, falling from paradise, has come into the captivity of this world, we shall see that all our thinking is toil and pain, and our beds are full of evils, and the very light that is seen is mixed with darkness, and what we plot at night we accomplish in gloom. For who of us lifts holy hands to God without anger and scheming? Who does not desire the estates of this world, forgetful of the possessions of paradise? You may see some joining field to field and boundary to boundary, and the lands of cities not sufficing for the small little body of a man.

I have expounded, as far as the narrow limits of my slender wit allowed, both the first captivity, by the Assyrians and Babylonians, and the second, by the Romans, because they crucified the Lord, and the third, the spiritual one, by which each one of us fell with Adam from paradise and lives in the captivity of this world; from which, when the Lord comes, he will raise up those who are crushed, and loose those in fetters, and lead back into his own possession those who were once the devil's captives, and the speech of the Psalmist will be fulfilled, who says: Ascending on high, he led captivity captive. […]

2:3.t: Since, therefore, you have done these things and devised what is useless, I too, the Lord, will devise evil against this family; not that what I devise is evil, but that what I inflict seems evil to those who suffer it; and it will so press upon you that you cannot lift your necks, nor walk proudly, you, namely, whom the time of captivity had oppressed.

Therefore the Lord devised evils against that tribe, by no means against the twelve tribes, but against the tribe of malice, befouled in crime, from which they could not lift their neck, nor walk upright. In short, to the present day they are subject to the Roman Empire, and are pressed down by the yoke of captivity, and do not lift their necks. As for what follows, ἐξαίφνης, that is, suddenly, it is not found in the Hebrew scrolls, and yet it can fit the present passage, so that we say: Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I devise evils against this tribe suddenly, from which they cannot lift their necks, and for this reason they will not be able to lift them, because the time is evil. […]

Therefore the Lord devises evils against us, from which we cannot lift our necks, nor walk upright, for it is a most evil time, according to the words of John, who says: The world is set in wickedness. The same thing is signified also by that daughter of Abraham in the Gospel, a noble soul, whom Satan had bound and bent over, and who could not be raised up on high before the coming of the Lord, nor look up at her Creator. Hence the Savior says: This woman, he says, a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan had bound, ought she not to have been loosed from this bond on the sabbath day?

2:4.t: Then a parable will be spoken over you, and your miseries will be turned into a song: We have been laid waste with devastation, the portion of my people. My temple, he says, which alone I had more than the other nations, will be changed into a ruin. How will the Assyrian depart from me, when he returns to distribute my fields to himself by lot? Therefore, O family of Israel, against which I devise evil, you will have no part in the inheritance of the just.

And the people will know how to say nothing else but this: In misery we have been made miserable. For the land of promise, which had earlier been divided by lot to two and a half tribes beyond the Jordan, with Moses casting the cord, and afterwards apportioned by Joshua son of Nun to the remaining tribes, has been divided among the nations by a Roman surveyor, and there was no one to forbid; rather, though it holds all the nations, there is no one of the Jews who possesses the ancient soil in its former freedom.

Since, therefore, all our glory has been shorn, and we have enlarged our shaving, or our widowhood — for so it is found in some codices —, men have been sent to mourn us with Jeremiah, and to take up a parable over us, and to say with the Apostle: I shall mourn many who have sinned and have not repented. For who would not mourn, seeing human souls possessed like assorted household goods by demons and various vices? One demon, that of fornication, casts the cord; another, that of avarice; that one, of murder; this one, of perjury, stretches out the lines. […]

2:6.t: Do not speak, speaking; it will not drip upon these, confusion will not overtake them, says the house of Jacob. Is the Spirit of the Lord cut short, or are such his thoughts? Are not my words good with him who walks uprightly? And on the contrary my people has risen up as an adversary; you have taken away the cloak from over the tunic, and those who were passing by in simplicity you have turned into war. LXX: In the Church of the Lord do not weep with tears, nor let them lament over these things? For he will not cast off the reproaches, which he speaks: The house of Jacob has provoked the Spirit of the Lord, if these are his devices; are not his words good with him, and have they walked upright? And formerly my people stood out with enmities against its own peace; […]

The Church, then, is commanded not to have sadness and anxiety over the affairs of the world and the losses that are wont to happen in this world, and it is said to her inhabitants: O you who are in the Church of the Lord, rejoice always, and whatever befalls you from the judgments of God, give thanks for it. Nor do I say this because you ought not to weep — for Blessed indeed are those who weep, for they shall laugh —, but I warn you of this, that you do not lament over the things that are of the world. […]

So much according to the Hebrew understanding; but the Seventy translators in this place do not cohere with themselves at all. For to what was set first, In the Church of the Lord do not weep, what consequence is there, that there should be added, for he will not cast off the reproaches which he speaks: The house of Jacob has provoked the Spirit of the Lord? And also what follows: If these are his devices, are not his words good with him, and have they walked upright? What bearing on the later part have the words that are said: And formerly my people stood out as an adversary against its own peace; they flayed off its skin, to take away the crushing of war? […]

2:7.t: But some one will say to me, You adduce a thing strange to me, when you call the Son the Word. For John indeed speaks of the Word, but it is by a figure of speech. Nay, it is by no figure of speech. For while thus presenting this Word that was from the beginning, and has now been sent forth, he said below in the Apocalypse, "And I saw heaven opened, and behold a white horse; and He that sat upon him (was) Faithful and True; and in righteousness He doth judge and make war. And His eyes (were) as flame of fire, and on His head were many crowns; and He had a name written that no man knew but He Himself. And He (was) clothed in a vesture dipped in blood: and His name is called the Word of God." […]

Will his generous mercy and his most clement Spirit, which has risen widely and abundantly upon all, be cut short and be severe in us alone? Or are his thoughts of such a kind as we see in men, so that he holds on to an old anger and is roused to vengeance by sudden fury? To this the Lord answered: I am indeed good, and my words sound clemency, but to those who walk on the right road.

There follows: If these are his devices: are not his words good with him, and have they walked upright? That the Jewish people stumbled, he says, so that the fullness of the Gentiles might come in, belongs to the dispensation of God, so that afterwards, when Israel believes, all might be saved, and all might stand in need of the mercy of God. Hence the Apostle too, coming to the question of this place, proclaims that the depth of the wisdom and knowledge and of the judgments of God is an unsearchable abyss. […]

2:8.t: But he who, I do not say long ago, but yesterday, worshipped idols in insult to me, and, as far as lay in him, seized tyrannical arms against me; who stripped the unhappy people of God's help, and took away the cloak as if from over the tunic; who turned against me in war all the simple among the believers and those who rest in the authority of their elders, will not the Lord drip upon him, and will not confusion seize him? But as for what we have translated, And on the contrary my people has risen up as an adversary, since the word mul signifies both the contrary and yesterday, Symmachus rendered it more plainly, so as to say: One day before, my people stood out as an enemy, in order to resolve the question, namely that God was imputing to the people not past vices but recent […]

And he himself, who is the true judge and speaks without perturbation, relates how in his passion Israel was contrary to him, and did this not because it could harm its Creator, but because it perpetrated everything against its own peace. Hence too the word to Jerusalem: If you knew the things that are for your peace. And with their peace lost, they flayed off their own skin, that is, they took away from themselves the help of God by which they were protected, and left their flesh as it were bare, without skin and covering, so that whatever seemed beautiful while the mercy of God covered it from above, this, when that mercy withdrew, displayed ugliness to those who saw it. […]

2:9.t: You have cast out the women of my people from the house of their delights; from their little ones you have taken away my praise forever. Arise and go, for you have no rest here; because of its uncleanness it will be corrupted with a most grievous rotting. The translation of the Seventy — if indeed it is the Seventy's; for Josephus writes, and the Hebrews hand down, that only the five books of the law of Moses were translated by them and handed over to King Ptolemy —, differs so much in the present place from the Hebrew truth that we can neither set out the heads side by side nor explain their meanings together. Therefore let our translation be discussed first, and afterwards we shall come to them. […]

LXX: The leaders of my people will be cast out of the houses of their delights; because of their evil devices they have been cast out. This can be taken both generally of the princes of the Jewish people, the priests and Pharisees, who after the passion of the Lord were cast out of the city of their delights, in which they had formerly wantoned because of their evil devices; and specially of the stock of David, because as soon as the Lord was born, the prince failed from Judah, and the leader from his thighs, when he came for whom it was reserved, and the expectation of the nations appeared. […]

LXX: Draw near to the eternal mountains. By the eternal mountains we can understand either angels or prophets, of whom it is also written in the psalm: Its foundations are on the holy mountains, and in another place: I have lifted up my eyes to the mountains, whence help will come to me. And he draws near to the eternal mountains who is not separated by his sins from the fellowship of the blessed, just as Moses too drew near to God, not in place but in merit. And to those who drew near to the eternal mountains the Lord himself spoke: I am a God who draws near, and not a God from afar. The mountains are called eternal to distinguish them from those which are not eternal, namely the princes of this world, the dark mountains; […]

2:10.t: Arise, therefore, and go into captivity, for you have no rest in this land, which has been polluted because of your crimes and cannot be cleansed unless it first keeps a long sabbath. And the reason I say to you, you have no rest here, is that your land is polluted and will be corrupted with a most grievous rotting, namely by captivity, either the Babylonian or the Roman, because it drank the blood of the Lord; for it can be understood according to either truth of the history.

LXX: Arise and walk, for there is no rest for you here. We are commanded to think that there is rest for us in none of the things of the world, but, as if rising from the dead, to strive toward the heights, and to walk after the Lord our God, and to say: My soul has cleaved after you. But if we despise this, and refuse to hear him who says, Arise, you who sleep, and be lifted up, and Christ will enlighten you; we shall indeed slumber, but we shall be deceived, and we shall not find rest, for where Christ does not enlighten the one who rises, what seems to be rest is tribulation.

LXX: Because of uncleanness you have been consumed with corruption. For what we have said, you have been consumed, it can, according to the Greek understanding, sound in the Latin language as you have been corrupted, so that the order is: because of uncleanness you have been corrupted with corruption. This is said to those who, serving the pleasure of the body and lust, corrupt not only their soul but their body as well, lovers of pleasures rather than lovers of God. He could also have said, because of uncleanness you have been corrupted, and the sense would have been complete even without with corruption. […]

LXX: You have fled with no one pursuing. This is said to those who because of uncleanness have been corrupted with corruption, that through the consciousness of their sins, even without punishments, they do not dare to resist the enemy and fight. Hence too those who are fearful in battle with the enemy, and would terrify the minds of their brothers, are cast out of the camp and driven from the battle line, and in the curses of Leviticus the word is directed to men of this kind: The sound of a flying leaf will pursue you, and you will flee, with no one pursuing. […]

2:11.t:
[Passage quoted, Micah ii. 11.]

Micah, too, agrees with the passages from Isaiah in stating that God will not receive all without qualification, but only those who are left. And as in Isaiah "their remnant" was called "a seed," so now those of them that are to be saved are called "a drop." And the choir of the apostles is shewn forth by those figures, as being a drop and a seed from the Jewish race, a drop from which all they that have known the Christ of God through the whole world and received His teaching, have been made worthy of the congregation foretold, having obtained redemption from their enemies.
2:11.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 2, Chapter 3

2:11.t: Would that I were not a man who has the spirit, and that I rather spoke a lie. I will drip for you into wine and into drunkenness, and this people will be the one upon whom it drips. Gathering I will gather Jacob, all of you; I will bring together into one the remnant of Israel alike. I will set him like a flock in the sheepfold, like cattle in the midst of the folds. They will be in tumult from the multitude of men; for he will go up opening the way before them; they will divide and pass through the gate and go out by it; and their king will pass on before them, and the Lord at their head. In this section too the Seventy translators differ much from the Hebrew. […]

LXX: The spirit has set a lie. It has dripped for you into wine and drunkenness, and it will be from the drop of this people; Jacob, to be gathered, will be gathered. It is not, as most suppose, the spirit stood false, but the spirit has set a lie that must be read, which in Greek is said πνεῦμα ἔστησε ψευδὲς, that is, τὸ ψεῦδος (the lie). For just as with putrid wounds, lest a cancer creep on and the dead body feed upon the living flesh, physicians arrest the wound and burn it with a cautery or with a καυστικῷ (caustic) powder, so the Spirit of God put an end to the lie, lest the people of God be any longer subverted by the voices of the false prophets. […]

To which state and condition of sonship when we have advanced, we shall forthwith be inflamed with the piety which belongs to good sons, so that we shall bend all our energies to the advance not of our own profit, but of our Father's glory, saying to Him: "Hallowed be Thy name," testifying that our desire and our joy is His glory, becoming imitators of Him who said: "He who speaketh of himself, seeketh his own glory. But He who seeks the glory of Him who sent Him, the same is true and there is no unrighteousness in Him." Finally the chosen vessel being filled with this feeling wished that he could be anathema from Christ if only the people belonging to Him might be increased and multiplied, and the salvation of the whole nation of Israel accrue to the glory of His Father; […]
2:11.s: The First Conference of Abbot Isaac, Chapter 18

2:12.t: LXX: With all, receiving I will receive the remnant from Israel. When, he says, the people of the Gentiles has believed, and the whole world has been brought to my faith, and the fullness of the Gentiles has entered, then the remnant of Israel too will be saved; not that remnant of which it is written in the book of Kingdoms, I have left for myself seven thousand men who have not bowed the knee to Baal, and of which Paul speaks, So also at this present time a remnant according to the election of grace has been saved, and of which this prophet testifies above, And it will be from the drop of this people; […]

LXX: I will set their turning away like sheep in tribulation. The remnant from Israel, which I am to receive after I have received all, I will now in the meantime, because they have turned away from me, set in tribulation, and straiten, and make to sit without priest, without altar and without prophet, so that him whom they did not perceive through benefits they may understand through punishments.

LXX: Like a flock in the midst of their resting place; I will set is understood. Not only, he says, will their turning away, by which they turned away from me, be set like a flock in tribulation, but after they have been afflicted and have completed the time of distress, they will be set in rest, that is, in their resting place. And then they will migrate from men and transcend the state of the human condition, and will fulfill what follows: They will leap forth from men. And not only will they leap forth and depart, but all to whom the word of God comes, and who, leaving human vices behind, imitate the way of life of the Godhead, and hear: I said, you are gods, and all sons of the Most High, they will leap forth from men, and will be borne, as it were, to heaven.

And lest you think that I am a prophet of evils only: now indeed the foretold captivity will come; but behold, in me speaks the word of God, which comes to all the prophets. When it is silent, the prophet does not speak; and now it says: I will come, and take a human body, I will be born of a virgin. Or thus: Because I came in the humility of the flesh and you did not believe me, I will come at the consummation of the world in my majesty with the angels and the other powers, and then I will gather all of you, Jacob; then I will bring together into one the remnant of Israel, and join them alike with the people of the Gentiles in my sheepfold; […]

2:13.t: LXX: Go up through the division. The present place has as it were its own exordium and an apostrophe of prophetic speech to him who desires to be saved, who is commanded to go up through the division. This indeed will become clearer if we take an example from Genesis, where twins are born of Tamar, with whom the patriarch Judah lay: It came to pass, it says, when she was giving birth, and had twins in her womb; in the very birth one put forth his hand, and the midwife tied scarlet on his hand, saying: This one will come out first. But when he had drawn back his hand, at once his brother came out, and she said: Why has the wall been divided for your sake? And she called his name Perez, which is interpreted division. […]

LXX: Before their face they divided and passed through the gate, and went out by it. And their king went out before their face. But the Lord is their leader. For this reason I said to you, Go up through the division, you who have risen with Christ and seek the things that are above: because the angels, or the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, divided what seemed to stand in the way, and made a way for those who wished to enter; and because, the road being open, they took to the road, they not only entered the gate, but also passed through it. And they entered because their king too entered the same gate and opened the way for them, so that they might walk without any difficulty. […]

3:1.t: For the Prophets ever rebuked them, saying, "Hear, ye rulers of Sodom"; and, "Thy rulers are disobedient"; and again, "Is it not for you to know judgment?" And everywhere they attack them vehemently. What then? Shall one blame God for this? Away with the thought. This blame is theirs. And what other proof can a man bring of your not knowing the Law than your not obeying it?

LXX: And he will say: Hear these things, O princes of the house of Jacob, and the rest of the house of Israel. The sentence clings to what went before. For above he had said: But the Lord will be the leader, and he will say: Hear, O princes of the house of Jacob, and the rest of the house of Israel. For "the rest of the house of Israel", all except the Seventy translated "leaders of the house of Israel". The Lord, therefore, who made a way for his people, and went out before their face, and is himself the leader of the journey of the simpler people, whom he calls his flock, threatens those who are unwilling to follow him as he goes before, but are proud, and, as judges of the people, do not follow his footsteps, and he says: Hear, O princes of the house of Jacob, and leaders of the […]

And I said: Hear, O princes of Jacob, and leaders of the house of Israel. Is it not yours to know judgment, you who hate the good and love evil, who violently tear their skins from off them, and their flesh from off their bones, who have eaten the flesh of my people, and flayed their skin from off them; and they have broken their bones, and chopped them up as in a cauldron, and like flesh in the midst of a pot. Then they will cry to the Lord, and he will not hear them, and he will hide his face from them at that time, as they have acted wickedly in their devices. The word is plainly directed against the princes of Israel, and under the metaphor of lions or of robbers their cruelty is described: that they despoiled the poor, and killed them, and crushed their flesh and bones; […]

3:2.t: LXX: Tearing away their skins from them, and their flesh from their bones. As they have devoured the flesh of my people, and flayed the skins from them, and broken their bones, and chopped them up like flesh in a cauldron, and like flesh in a pot; so will they cry to the Lord, and he will not hear them, and he will turn away his face from them at that time, because they have acted most wickedly in their devices. It had not been enough for them to despoil the flock subject to them, but they also afflicted their bodies with harsh rule, and crushed their bones, so as to break and grind whatever perhaps had been in them. […]

3:5.t: But if we choose to take what is said according to the Seventy as concerning the heretics, who are truly false prophets, and say, thus says the Lord, when the Lord has not sent them, we shall not err. For they deceive the people that was once God's with error, and they do this in order to eat them, either simply in receiving presents, or mystically in the slaughter of their souls; and they promise them peace and the heavenly kingdoms, and say, there is no need for you to live continently and holily; hold the faith which we teach, and you will obtain all the promises of the Lord. Speaking such things, they rather stir up the wrath of the Lord against them, and sanctify war against them.

Thus says the Lord concerning the prophets who lead my people astray, who bite with their teeth and preach peace; and if anyone does not put something into their mouth, they sanctify war against him; therefore night shall be to you instead of vision, and darkness to you instead of divination, and the sun shall go down upon the prophets, and the day shall be darkened over them, and those who see visions shall be confounded; and the diviners shall be confounded, and they shall all cover their faces, because there is no answer of God. But I am filled with the strength of the spirit of the Lord, with judgment and truth, to declare to Jacob his crime, and to Israel his sin. […]

3:6.t: Wherefore, O you heretics, who think that you have prophecy and imitate the Church of God, where you suppose there is vision, there will be night, and where you boast of prophetic utterance, there the unclean spirit will speak. For the sun of justice will set upon prophets of this kind, and they will see their own darkness and be confounded. And when they have been proved to be diviners rather than prophets, they will be laughed at over their dreams, and the peoples who had formerly been deceived by them will speak against them. Then the teachers themselves too will repent, and no one will hear them except I, whom they had offended. […]

3:8.t: If, further, one works through the twelve minor prophets, many testimonies to the Holy Spirit are to be found. Thus Micah speaks as God's mouthpiece and says, "Truly I am full of power by the Spirit of the Lord." Joel cries, " 'And it shall come to pass afterwards,' says God, 'that I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh' " and what follows. Haggai said, " 'For I am with you,' says the Lord of hosts … 'my Spirit remained among you.' " And in like manner Zechariah says, "Receive my words and my statutes which I commanded my servants the prophets."

Again the speech of the prophet speaking about himself is introduced: while they prophesy falsely and are covered with confusion and ignominy, I, what I speak, I speak moved by the Holy Spirit, and I speak the judgment of the Lord and the truth. And while the false prophets bite with their teeth and preach peace, I without any fear declare to Jacob his crime and to Israel his sin, because they either worshipped idols in place of God, or crucified the Son of God.

The third ground of the influx of fortitude is from God indwelling. Whence in Micah: "I am filled with the fortitude of the Lord, with judgment and power." The human body, when it does not have a spirit, does not have power, even if it were a gigantic body; so if God is not in the soul, then it does not have power.

3:9.t: And all this it says will come to pass because of the sin of the house of Jacob, and the transgression of the house of Israel. And it goes on to describe this sin and transgression, "They that defile judgment and pervert all that is right, who build Sion with blood and Jerusalem with unrighteousness." With blood! Yes, this was the cause of their final misery, for that they pronounced the impious curse upon themselves, saying, "His blood be on us and on our children."
3:9.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 8, Chapter 3

3:9.t: The judges and princes of the house of Jacob and of the house of Israel, that is, of both the two and the ten tribes, not only did not do judgment, but abhorred it, and perverted all that is right, so that not even a little justice might remain in the city, because they built Zion with bloodshed, and Jerusalem with iniquity, with the plundering of the poor, the slaughter of the innocent, the killing of the saints.

But if anyone transfers these things which are said of Jerusalem and of Zion to the Church (for she is the house of Jacob and the house of Israel, according to what is written in Isaiah: Jacob my servant, I will uphold him, and that word to Timothy: That you may know how you ought to conduct yourself in the house of God, which is the Church), he will see clearly that the princes of the house of Jacob, and the rest of the house of Israel, or, as is better written in the Hebrew: judges of the house of Israel, are none other than the bishops, presbyters and deacons, who, unless they have kept their heart with all watchfulness, abhor judgment and pervert all that is right; […]

Hear these things, O princes of the house of Jacob, and judges of the house of Israel, you who abhor judgment and pervert all that is right, who build Zion with bloodshed, and Jerusalem with iniquity. Her princes judged for gifts, and her priests taught for hire, and her prophets divined for money; and they leaned upon the Lord, saying: Is not the Lord in our midst? No evils will come upon us. Therefore, because of you, Zion will be plowed like a field, and Jerusalem will be like a heap of stones, and the mountain of the temple like the high places of the forests. LXX: Hear these things, O judges of the house of Jacob and the rest of the house of Israel, you who abhor judgment and pervert all that is right; who build Zion with bloodshed, and Jerusalem with iniquities. […]

3:10.t: Hence again the divine Micah, unable to brook the building of Zion with blood, however you interpret the phrase, and of Jerusalem with iniquity, while the heads thereof judge for reward, and the priests teach for hire, and the prophets divine for money—what does he say will be the result of this? Zion shall be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem be as a lodge in a garden, and the mountain of the house be reckoned as a glade in a thicket.

3:11.t: And if any of the princes seemed to judge what was right, he rather sold his sentence, and judged for gifts. The priests also did not teach the people unless they had received a price; and whereas it is said to the saints: Freely you have received, freely give, they, bringing forth the answer of God when money had been received, sold the grace of the Lord for avaricious hire. And after these evils, not understanding their sin, as though they were buying back the love of God with crimes, they kept declaring that they were judges and priests and prophets of God, and in accordance with their impenitent heart they said: The Lord is in our midst, and no evils will come upon us.

And although the prophet Malachi calls priests angels, and their mouth is the oracle of the Lord, they do not judge without the taking of gifts, though they read: Gifts blind the eyes even of the wise, and like a bridle in the mouth turn away reproof. And although it is said to the apostles: Do not possess gold and silver, nor let there be copper in your belts; and money, even when earned by labor, is to be shaken out of the hands of a holy man, they sell the words of the Lord and trade in doves in the temple. But the prophets of Jerusalem also divined for money, not knowing that prophecy is one thing and divination another; for divination is never taken in a good sense in the Scriptures. There shall be, he says, no augury in Jacob, nor divination in Israel. […]

If however circumvention occurs with a profane agreement, it is called simony, in which he who buys acquires nothing, nor does he who sells possess anything, but they only handle another's property: and this happens when a spiritual thing is sold as though it were a cheap thing. Against whom the Lord says: "Do not make my Father's house a house of trade." But some make it a den of thieves; whence: "Her princes judged for bribes, and her priests taught for hire, and her prophets divined for money."

3:12.t:
"Sion shall be ploughed as a field, and Jerusalem shall be as a granary, and the mount of the house as a grove of the wood."

Sion and Jerusalem and the so-called "mount of the house" are what were represented before in, "And the mountains shall be shaken from beneath him, and the valleys shall be melted as wax before the fire for the iniquity of Jacob." For the mountains and the dwellers thereon were besieged for the iniquity they had wrought against Him soon and not long after Mount Sion was burned and left utterly desolate, and the Mount of the House of God became as a grove of the wood. 3:12.t: Therefore, it says this, "Zion shall be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem shall be as a storehouse of fruit," a prophecy which was only actually fulfilled after the impious treatment of our Saviour. For from that time to this utter desolation has possessed the land; their once famous Mount Sion, instead of being, as once it was, the centre of study and education based on the divine prophecies, which the children of the Hebrews of old, their godly prophets, priests and national teachers loved to interpret, is a Roman farm like the rest of the country, yea, with my own eyes I have seen the bulls plowing there, and the sacred site sown with seed. And Jerusalem itself is become but a storehouse of its fruit of old days now destroyed, or better, as the Hebrew has it, a stone-quarry. […]
3:12.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 8, Chapter 3

3:12.t: Isaiah lived almost a thousand years ago and saw Zion in its primitive form. The city was still standing, beautified with public squares and clothed in honor; yet he says, "Zion shall be plowed like a field." He was foretelling what has been fulfilled in our day. Observe the exactness of the prophecy; for he said, "Daughter Zion shall be left like a hut in a vineyard, like a shed in a cucumber patch." Now the place is full of cucumber patches. Do you see how the Holy Spirit enlightens the saints? Therefore do not be distracted by a common term but hold fast to what is exactly true.

Since, therefore, they did not repent, and the whole people followed the vices of the princes and priests and prophets, Zion will be plowed like a field, and Jerusalem will be like a heap of stones, and the temple, which formerly shone with gold and silver, will collapse into utter ruins. These things are against the people of the Jews, upon whom the true captivity and the final ruins were imposed, on account indeed of their earlier crimes, but chiefly on account of the shedding of the Lord's blood. Hence too Zion has been plowed like a field, and Jerusalem turned into mounds of stones, and that temple, once noble and lofty, has been ground down into the last ashes.

Therefore, because of us, who are such, who build Zion with blood, and Jerusalem with iniquity, who judge for gifts, who give answers for hire, who divine for money, and who, claiming besides a feigned sanctity for ourselves, say: No evils will come upon us. Let us hear the sentence of the Lord which follows: Zion and Jerusalem, and the mountain of the temple, the watchtower, and the vision of peace, and the temple of Christ, at the consummation and at the end, when charity has grown cold and faith has become rare, will be plowed like a field, and will be reduced to mounds, and will be like the high places of the forests, or a watch-hut for fruit, so that where once there were spacious houses and heaps of grain without number, there there may scarcely be a little hut keeping the […]

And there rose up men of the elders of the land and said to the whole assembly of the people, speaking: Micah of Moresheth was a prophet in the days of Hezekiah, king of Judah, and he spoke to all the people of Judah, saying: Thus says the Lord of hosts: Zion shall be plowed like a field, and Jerusalem shall become a heap of stones, and the mountain of the house the heights of the forests. Did Hezekiah, king of Judah, and all Judah condemn him to death? Did they not fear the Lord and entreat the face of the Lord, and the Lord repented of the evil which he had spoken against them? So we are doing a great evil against our own souls. The princes of the city and the people understand the truth of the judgment; […]

4:1.t: These things are open for the eyes to see, and it should be clear as well that it is hence that the new law and word of the new Covenant of our Saviour Jesus Christ goes forth. For countless companies of people, races of all kinds deserting their fathers' gods and their old superstitions, call on the Supreme God. And thus it is reckoned the deepest peace, there being no diversity of government or national rule, that nation should not take up sword against nation, and that they should not learn war any more, but that each farmer should rest under his vine and under his fig tree, according to the prophecy, and that none should make him afraid. […]
4:1.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 8, Chapter 3

4:1.t: And it shall be in the last of days, there shall be the mountain of the house of the Lord, prepared on the top of the mountains, and lofty above the hills; and peoples shall flow to it; and many nations shall hasten, and they shall say: Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, and to the house of the God of Jacob, and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths, for out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem; and he shall judge among many peoples, and rebuke strong nations even afar off; and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into mattocks; nation shall not take up sword against nation, and they shall not learn to make war any more; […]

On my holy mountain, on the high mountain of Israel, says the Lord God, there all the house of Israel shall serve me: all, I say, in the land in which they shall please me; and there I will require your firstfruits and the beginning of your tithes in all your sanctifications. In an odor of sweetness I will receive you, when I have led you out from the peoples and gathered you from the lands into which you were scattered, and I shall be sanctified in you in the eyes of the nations. And you shall know that I am the Lord. Of this mountain, on which all the house of Israel is to serve God, Isaiah and Micah sang with one voice: In the last days the mountain of the house shall be manifest on the summit of the mountains and shall be raised above the hills; […]

It must also be known that the Jews and the heirs of their error refer both this section which we have now expounded and the one like it in Isaiah to the thousand-year reign of Christ and of the saints; and that what is said: All peoples shall walk, each in the name of the Lord his God, they interpret in this way: that each nation is to be tormented with its idol and sent into the fire of eternal punishment. But they are refuted by what follows: this is said not of the end of the ages but of the first coming of Christ, in which the remnant of her that halts is gathered, and the nations are saved first. […]

The prophet Micah employed the symbol of a high mountain to speak of the gathering of the nations in Christ. He has this to say: "And it shall come to pass in the last days that the mountain of the house of the Lord shall be prepared in the top of the mountains and high above the hills; and people shall flow to it. And many nations shall come in haste, and say, 'Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, and to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths; for the law shall go forth out of Zion, and the word of the Lord out of Jerusalem. And he shall judge among many people and rebuke strong nations afar off.' "

4:2.t: And when the Spirit of prophecy speaks as predicting things that are to come to pass, He speaks in this way: "For out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem. And He shall judge among the nations, and shall rebuke many people; and they shall beat their swords into ploughshares, and their spears into pruning-hooks: nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more." And that it did so come to pass, we can convince you. For from Jerusalem there went out into the world, men, twelve in number, and these illiterate, of no ability in speaking: but by the power of God they proclaimed to every race of men that they were sent by Christ to teach to all the word of God; […]

And while the peoples hasten, very many nations also shall go to the mountain, namely the whole world believing in him, and they shall say, calling one another to the standard of the gibbet: Come, let us go up into the mountain of the Lord. There is need of an ascent for anyone to be able to reach Christ, to the house of the God of Jacob, the Church, which is the house of God, the pillar and foundation of the truth. Moreover, that Jacob signifies the Savior we have also said above: Jacob my servant, I will receive him. And they will say this also to those to whom they had spoken: Come, let us go up into the mountain of the Lord and into the house of the God of Jacob, and they will add: That they may show us his way; […]

4:3.t: The Father indeed has given all judgment to the Son. And he will rebuke strong nations even afar off. For the Lord catches the wise in their craftiness and has known the thoughts of the wise, that they are vain. And he discerns among the peoples who are worthy of salvation and who unworthy, and at his coming all eagerness for war will be turned to peace. Swords will be changed into plows, spears will be forged into sickles, nation will cease to war against nation. No one will learn to fight, the need of fighting being laid aside. And so great will be the rest that not only in the cities but in the hamlets too and in the fields each one will be secure; and this will come to pass because the mouth of the Lord has spoken. […]

4:4.t: He is indeed the field blessed by the Lord: not this earthly one, or rough with woods, or rocky with torrents, or marshy with stagnant waters, or barren of crops, or useless for vines, or infertile with stony gravel, or gaping and dry from drought, or soaked with blood, or uncultivated with thorns and brambles: but that field, of which the Church says in the Canticles: I have adjured you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the powers and fortitude of the field. For this is the field of which the Lord says: 'And the appearance of the field is with me'. In this field is found that grape which, when pressed, shed blood and cleansed the world. In this field is that fig tree under which the saints will rest, refreshed by the sweetness of spiritual grace. […]
4:4.s: On Jacob and the Blessed Life

4:4.t: These are the mysteries of Scripture. Who can conceive the charm of the mysteries of Sacred Scriptures of which it is said: "Every one under his vine and under his fig tree."

4:5.t: All peoples shall go, each in his own way, but we will walk in the name of the Lord our God unto the age and beyond. While all the nations, they say, go according to their own error, we have hastened to the mountain of the Lord, and have said: Come, let us go up into the mountain of the Lord, and into the house of the God of Jacob and we will walk in the name of Christ our Lord, for he himself is the mountain who is God.

5:2.t: It is enough for piety for you to know, as we have said, that God has one only Son, one naturally begotten, who did not begin to be when he was born in Bethlehem but is before all ages. For listen to the prophet Micah: "And you, Bethlehem, house of Ephratha, are little to be among the thousands of Judah. From you shall come forth for me a leader who shall feed my people Israel; and his goings forth are from the beginning, from the days of eternity." Therefore do not fix your attention on him as coming from Bethlehem simply but worship him as begotten eternally of the Father. Admit no one who speaks of a beginning of the Son in time, but acknowledge his timeless beginning, the Father.

And you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, are little among the thousands of Judah; out of you shall come forth for me one who is to be ruler in Israel, and his going forth is from the beginning, from the days of eternity. LXX: And you, Bethlehem, house of Ephrathah, are least, that you should be among the thousands of Judah; out of you shall come forth for me one who is to be prince of Israel, and his going forth is from the beginning, from the days of the age. In the Gospel according to Matthew, when the Magi had come from the east and Herod asked the scribes where Christ the Lord was to be born, they are related to have answered: In Bethlehem in the land of Judah, and, adding the prophet's testimony, they said: And you, Bethlehem, land of Judah, are by no means least among the princes of […]

Further, the same prophet foretold even the place in which Christ was to be born: "But you, O Bethlehem Eph'rathah, who are little among the clans of Judah, from you shall come forth for me one who is to be ruler in Israel, whose origin is from old, from ancient days."

By designating Bethlehem, they [the Jews] were like the builders of Noah's ark, providing others the means of escape, yet themselves perishing in the flood. Like milestones, they showed the way but were incapable of walking along it. They were asked where the Christ was to be born. They answered, "In Bethlehem of Judah. For thus it was written by the prophet"—they were repeating from memory, you see, what had been written about this by Micah: "And you, Bethlehem, land of Judah, are not the least among the leaders of Judah; for from you shall come forth the king who is going to be the shepherd of my people Israel."

According to prophecy, Christ was born in Bethlehem of Judah, at the time, as I said, when Herod was king in Judea. At Rome, the republic had given way to the entire empire, and the emperor Caesar Augustus had established a worldwide peace. Christ was born a visible man of a virgin mother, but he was a hidden God because God was his Father. So the prophet had foretold: "Behold, the virgin shall be with child and shall bring forth a son; and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which is interpreted, God with us." To prove that he was God, Christ worked many miracles, some of which—as many as seemed necessary to establish his claim—are recorded in the Gospels. Of these miracles the very first was the marvelous manner of his birth.

And it is written again, "And you Bethlehem, the house of Ephrata, are small to be among the thousands of Judah: out of you shall He come forth for Me Who shall be the Head of Israel." For Bethlehem was indeed small, and in comparison with the general populousness of the Jews, its inhabitants were very few; yet from it came forth Christ, as having been born in it of the holy virgin: not as one subject to the shadows of the law, but rather as ruler both over the law and the prophets.

5:2.t: And so the three men aroused by God through the shining of a strange star, follow the guidance of its twinkling light, thinking they will find the babe designated at Jerusalem in the royal city. But finding themselves mistaken in this opinion, through the scribes and teachers of the Jews they learnt what the Holy Scripture had foretold of the birth of Christ; so that confirmed by a twofold witness, they sought with still more eager faith Him whom both the brightness of the star and the sure word of prophecy revealed. And when the Divine oracle was proclaimed through the chief priests’ answers and the Spirit’s voice declared, which says: “And thou, Bethlehem, the land of Judah, art not least among the princes of Judah; […]

This is Micah the seventh in order, who also was privileged to prophesy concerning the coming of the Lord Christ, and he says: And thou Bethlehem, the house of Ephratha, art the least to be among the thousands of Judah. From thee, there shall come forth to me one who shall be for a ruler over Israel, whose goings forth have been of old from everlasting. The chief priests and scribes of the Jews, taking this passage, when Herod asked them where the Christ should be born, replied, In Bethlehem of Judaea, upon which he sent the Wise Men away to Bethlehem.

And to this day the inhabitants of the place, who have received the tradition from their fathers, confirm the truth of the story by shewing to those who visit Bethlehem because of its history the cave in which the Virgin bare and laid her infant, as the prophecy says:

"Therefore he shall give them until the time of her that brings forth: She shall bring forth, and the rest of their brethren shall turn to them."

And by "her that brings forth "he means accordingly her that in the former prophecies was called a Virgin, and the prophetess who was delivered of Emmanuel and the Angel of Great Counsel. […]

LXX: Therefore he will give them up until the time of her who brings forth: she shall bring forth, and the remnant of the brothers shall return to the sons of Israel. Because Christ, the ruler in Israel, came forth from Bethlehem which is Ephrathah, and his going forth had not been only at the time when he was seen in the flesh, but from the beginning of eternity, or from the beginning of the age. But now, the same star which led the magi to the place where the infant God was to be found with his virgin mother could of course have led them right to the very city. But it withdrew, and didn't appear at all to them again, until the Jews themselves had been questioned about the city where Christ was to be born. "Hear all peoples, and let the earth attend, and all that are therein, and the Lord shall be a witness to you, the Lord from his holy house. Wherefore behold the Lord, the Lord comes forth from his place, and shall descend,"

But it is clear, from what the same prophet goes on to say, that it was not only because of the sin of the Jews, that the Lord came down, but also for the salvation and calling of all nations. […]

After the sun of justice has gone forth from the height of the heavens and has come to their ends, and she who brings forth has brought forth, and the remnant of his brothers has been converted to the sons of Israel, then the Lord himself, who before was walking, and, together with those who were set on the road, did not yet have a fixed step, will stand and feed them in the strength of the […]

But one must start fresh in considering that which succeeds it, which runs thus:

"When the Assyrian shall attack your land, and come against your country, there shall be raised up against him seven shepherds, and eight 'bites' of men,"

with that which follows, whose meaning we are not now called upon to unfold.

Now it might be said that after the expedition of the Assyrians into Judaea, when they overcame the Jews, the number of rebellions against them is shewn by the seven shepherds and the eight "bites": and that historians of Assyria would know this, and at the end of their rule the one foretold was born at Bethlehem, after the seven shepherds and the eight "bites" had happened to the Assyrians in the period after their expedition against Judaea. 5:5.t: And this one shall be peace: when the Assyrian comes into our land, and when he treads in our houses. LXX: And this shall be peace: when the Assyrian comes upon your land, and when he goes up upon your country. When the devil, who is interpreted εὐθύνων, that is, reproving and rebuking, comes upon the land and country of believers, and of those whom the Lord will feed in strength and in the loftiness of the name of the Lord his God, and treads them down with various tribulations, and like a proud man goes up upon the houses of our souls, that is, our bodies, and presses them down, and yet nothing separates us from the love of Christ; then the peace of Christ, or Christ himself, will be in us, and it will be said of the saint: The enemy shall gain nothing over him. […]

Then, therefore, there will be peace, when the remnant of Christ's brothers has been converted to the sons of Israel, and the Assyrian has come into our land, and, helped by the Lord, we have swiftly crushed under our feet him who desired to tread our houses. For the Lord himself says: We shall raise up against him seven shepherds, and eight principal ones of men, or bites of men. And we shall raise up, I and my Son and the Holy Spirit, according to what is written in Genesis: Let us make man after our image and likeness. And at the beginning of Obadiah: Arise, and let us go up against her to battle. The seven shepherds I take to be all the patriarchs and prophets and holy men who served the hebdomad, that is, the old instrument. […]

And we shall raise up against him seven shepherds, and eight principal men. And they shall feed the land of Asshur with the sword, and the land of Nimrod with its lances; and he shall deliver from Asshur when he comes into our land, and when he treads within our borders. LXX: And seven shepherds shall rise up against him, and eight bites of men; and they shall feed Asshur with the sword, into the land of Nimrod in its pit; and he shall deliver from Asshur, when he comes upon your land, and when he goes up upon your borders. Where we have put principal men, and in the Hebrew is written nesiche adam, Symmachus rendered christs (anointed ones) of men; Theodotion and the Fifth Edition, princes of men; Aquila, weighty, or established men, that is, καθεσταμένους. 5:6.t: These seven shepherds, then, and eight bites of men, shall feed Asshur with the sword. For the word of God, living and effective, and sharper than any two-edged sword, was sent by him who came to send a sword upon the earth, so that two might be divided against three. And the land of Nimrod, which means temptation descending, they shall feed in its pit; for the land of the giant and hunter, and of him who is proud against the Lord, is not on the mountains but in pits. He fell like lightning from heaven, and is always busy among the beasts; and because he is a hunter, he roams the fruitless trees and the forests. So far, then, as I can recall in my memory, I have never read of a hunter in a good sense. […]

5:7.t: And the remnant of Jacob shall be in the midst of many peoples, like dew from the Lord, and like drops upon the grass, which does not wait for man, and does not tarry for the sons of men. And the remnant of Jacob shall be among the nations, in the midst of many peoples, like a lion among the beasts of the forests, and like a lion's whelp among the flocks of cattle, which, when it has passed through and trampled and seized, there is none to rescue. Your hand shall be exalted over your foes, and all your enemies shall perish. […]

But the Hebrews dream ravings of this kind: after the seven shepherds, whom they invent and choose at will, and eight princely men have conquered the Assyrians and have fed upon the land of Nimrod with their swords, so that this shall have happened when the Assyrian has first come into the land of Judah, then, they say, when Christ comes, all the remnant of Jacob that has been able to survive among the nations will be in blessing, like dew coming from the Lord and like rain upon the grass, and they will by no means hope in men and in the sons of men, but in God. And it says lower down :

"And the remnant of Jacob shall be among the nations in the midst of many peoples, as a lion among the cattle of the forest, and as a lion's whelp in the pastures of sheep; as when he goes through, and chooses, and spoils, and there is none to save."

By which I think is meant the bravery and intrepidity of the apostles' preaching. They threw themselves like a lion and a lion's whelp on the thicket of the Gentiles and on the flocks of human sheep, they parted the worthy from the unworthy, and subjected them to the word of Christ.

And then His victories are proclaimed to Him : "Thy hand shall be exalted against them that trouble thee, and all thy enemies shall be destroyed."

And we can see this with our own eyes. […]

5:9.t: And as the lion and the lion's whelp thus range among the beasts and among the sheep, the hand of God is exalted over those who before afflicted either God or the remnant of Israel. And all his enemies will be destroyed, not that the enemies perish and cease to exist, but that they perish in that they are enemies. As it is written to the Thessalonians: Whom the Lord Jesus will kill with the spirit of his mouth. This killing signifies not abolition but the cessation of the most wicked life by which they had lived badly before. In short, he adds: And he will destroy him by the brightness of his coming. But he would never destroy him if killing meant abolition, since he would already have ceased to exist; […]

But they certainly have to labour, and when they attack men, exert themselves in no lesser degree in order to secure from each one that victory which they want to obtain, and there is hurled back upon them the same confusion which was awaiting us had we been worsted by them; as it is said: "The head of their compassing me about, the labour of their own lips shall overwhelm them;" and: "His sorrow shall be turned on his own head;" and again: "Let the snare which he knoweth not come upon him, and let the net which he hath hidden catch him, and into that very snare let him fall;" viz., that which he contrived for the deception of men.
